answer: Require every new identity to pass through a public prism of scrutiny: registration enters a cooling-off voyage during which its claimed history is published in an open atlas of identities, and any peer may file a bonded duplication challenge with evidence. A valid challenge revokes all clones and pays the challenger from the Sybil's bond, while a false challenge forfeits the challenger's own bond. Cloning then costs a fresh bond per copy plus the risk of total loss, while honest newcomers lose only time, since their single record survives unchallenged.
